Why this matters for SSC

"X dance is from Y country" — 1 mark question, often paired with the Indian dance chapter. Common asks: Tango, Waltz, Flamenco, Salsa, etc.

---

Dances classified by type

Classical (formal) Indian — 9 forms

(Per Ministry of Culture: 9 classical. Per Sangeet Natak Akademi: 8.)

  • Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu)
  • Kathak (North India)
  • Kathakali (Kerala)
  • Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh)
  • Odissi (Odisha)
  • Manipuri (Manipur)
  • Mohiniyattam (Kerala)
  • Sattriya (Assam)
  • Chhau (added by Ministry of Culture, 2008)

Latin American Dances

  • Tango, Samba, Rumba, Mambo, Cha-Cha-Cha, Salsa, Bachata, Merengue, Cumbia, Lambada, Capoeira.

Ballroom (International Standard)

  • Waltz, Viennese Waltz, Foxtrot, Tango, Quickstep.

Ballroom (International Latin)

  • Cha-Cha-Cha, Samba, Rumba, Paso Doble, Jive.

2024–2025 Updates

  • Classical Indian dance count (9 as of 2024): Sangeet Natak Akademi recognises 8 classical forms (Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Sattriya); the Ministry of Culture added Chhau in 2008, making it 9 official classical dances of India. (No new addition in 2024–25.)
  • Garba — UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (2023): Garba of Gujarat was added to the UNESCO ICH list in 2023 — confirmed for 2024–25 SSC GK. (See 18 - UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India for full ICH list.)
  • Bharatanatyam / Kathak — the most-asked Indian classical dances. No change in 2024–25.
  • World Dances — no new "national dance" was added or removed in 2024–25.
For SSC 2025: Lock in the 9 classical Indian dances; the country-to-dance mappings (Tango-Argentina, Waltz-Austria, etc.) remain the same.
